About Our Premium Golden Raisins

Raisins are made by dehydrating green grapes. In most raisins, the drying process oxidizes the grapes and the raisins end up a dark brown/purple/black color. They are left with a warm, malted, honey taste. However, a few varieties like Muscata, Black Monukka, or Sultana keep their light tan color. They have slightly brighter, fruity sweetness to them. The raisins have been dried to the point that they have less than 19% moisture by weight. They have a light golden color, sweet caramel-like flavor, and soft chewy texture. All-natural with no sugar added, a delicious and healthy snack.

Benefits of Raisins

Raisins contain four times the fiber, minerals, and vitamins of fresh grapes. Packed with fiber and potassium as well as powerful antioxidants. Raisins may improve your digestive health and blood sugar levels, decrease inflammation, and lower your blood pressure; however, they should be eaten in moderation because they are high in sugar and calories. Raisins are a useful addition to savory dishes that would benefit from one sweet flavor note. Brussels sprouts, sautéed spinach, and roasted cauliflower are all vegetables that are complimented by raisins.

Storing Raisins

Golden raisins have a very long and stable shelf life if stored in a cool, dry place.

description:
History of Blueberries Plants

Who doesn’t love blueberries? They are sweet, juicy, and taste incredible in muffins. They are also rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants, which makes these berries one of the delicioust foods you can find.

There are many different types of blueberries plants. They are often called different names and grow all over the world. However, the fruits that are considered ‘blueberries’ in the world of commercial deals, are native to the North America. Here they grow freely and you can still find quite a few bushes producing tasty berries in the wild.

These blueberries have been an exclusively American treasure for a very long time. They only traveled to Europe in the 1930s, but today they are grown in South America, New Zealand, and Australia as well.

The US remains the main producer of blueberries in the world, and Washington is the leader among the states with over 96 million tons of berries produced there every year. Michigan and Georgia are close in their supply rates, but every state grows at least some variety of local blueberries plants, be they cultivated or ‘wild’.

Wild blueberries are smaller, but they are also sold commercially. These berries are harvested from managed, but natural growth areas of the shrubs.

The people of today can thank Frederic Coville and Elizabeth White for the blueberries plants that produce large fruits. In 1910, they started a cultivation program that encouraged everyone to grow their own variety of blueberries, and we get to enjoy its results.

At Food To Live, we source our Organic Dried Blueberries from the top-rated farmers and ensure that they are processed with utmost care. Our USDA facility adheres to the high safety standards maintained in the US .

title: Jansal Valley Dried Apricots, 8 oz
bullet_point: [One of our most popular dried fruit, Deliciously sweet, Perfect for baking or snacking, Kosher]
description:
Our Jansal Valley Dried Apricots begin by using the best fresh fruit handpicked from the world’s finest farms. By using the highest quality ingredients, the fruits natural flavor and sweetness require little else to shine all year round. Apple, Cranberry and Jansal Valley Dried Apricot Chutney. Makes: Approx. 2-3 Cups Chutney’s are perfect for preserving fruit at the peak of season and flavor. Adding Jansal Valley Dried Apricots gives this chutney a natural sweetness and creamy texture. Try this chutney on a ham sandwich or as an elegant homemade condiment on your table. T Olive Oil. 3 T Shallots / minced. 1 ½ t Garlic / thinly sliced. 2 t Ginger Pinch of Crushed Red Pepper Flakes Pinch of Salt. 4 C Turbinado Sugar. 3/4 C Raspberry Vinegar. ½ Cup Water. 2 Heaping Cups Apple / peeled and roughly chopped / about 2 apples. 1 Cup Jansal Valley Dried Apricots. 1 Cup Fresh Cranberries. Optional: Parchment Paper. In a medium sauce pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add shallots and sauté until translucent. Add garlic, ginger, pepper flakes and salt, sauté another 2 minutes. Add sugar and sauté another 3 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in the vinegar and water. Return to the stovetop, and add in the remaining ingredients. Cover with parchment paper* or lid and simmer on very low heat for 40 minutes, or until apples are cooked through and are tender. At this point, remove the lid and simmer until the mixture is thick and almost all of the extra liquid has evaporated. Cool on the countertop, transfer to glass jars, seal, and store in the refrigerator up to two weeks. Tip: Parchment paper lids are beneficial because they balance the moisture when you’re cooking food on the stove top. They help keep in flavor and some moisture like a full lid, but also allow for excess moisture to escape – this will result in a richly flavored, slowly cooked chutney. To construct your own tear off a square from your parchment paper roll (bigger in size then your pan’s diameter). Lay the paper flat. Fold it down in half towards you. Then take the left side and fold it in half over the right. Now fold the right corners to meet each other. It should look like a triangle (think of this like you’re making a decorative snow flake). Cut the tip off (about a ¼” will do - this allows ventilation of the steam in the middle) and measure it in your pot to see how much should be cut from the other end. The lid should fit perfectly in your pot so it sits on top of the chutney.

Nuestros albaricoques secos de Jansal Valley comienzan usando la mejor fruta fresca seleccionada a mano de las mejores granjas del mundo. Mediante el uso de ingredientes de la más alta calidad, el sabor natural de las frutas y dulzura requieren poco más para brillar durante todo el año. Manzana, Arándano y Jansal Valley Dried Chutney de albaricoque. Marca: Aprox. 2-3 tazas de Chutney son perfectas para preservar la fruta en el pico de temporada y sabor. Agregar albaricoques secos de Jansal Valley le da a este chutney una dulzura natural y textura cremosa. Prueba este chutney en un sándwich de jamón o como un elegante condimento casero en tu mesa. T Aceite de Oliva. 3 T chalotes / picado. 1 ½ t de ajo/rodajas finas. 2 t Pellizco de jengibre de escamas de pimiento rojo triturado pellizco de sal. Azúcar Turbinado 4C. Vinagre de frambuesa 3/4C. ½ taza de agua. 2 tazas de manzana, peladas y picadas, aproximadamente 2 manzanas. 1 taza de albaricoques secos del valle de Jansal. 1 taza de arándanos frescos. Opcional: Papel de pergamino. En una sartén de salsa media, caliente el aceite de oliva a fuego medio. Añadir chalotes y saltear hasta que quede translúcido. Agregue el ajo, el jengibre, los copos de pimienta y la sal, saltee otros 2 minutos. Agregue el azúcar y saltee otros 3 minutos. Retire del fuego, revuelva el vinagre y el agua. Vuelva a la estufa y agregue los ingredientes restantes. Cubra con papel pergamino* o tapa y cocine a fuego lento durante 40 minutos, o hasta que las manzanas se cocinen y estén tiernas. En este punto, retire la tapa y cocine a fuego lento hasta que la mezcla esté gruesa y casi todo el líquido extra se haya evaporado. Enfriar en la encimera, transferir a frascos de vidrio, sellar y almacenar en el refrigerador hasta dos semanas. Consejo: Las tapas de papel pergamino son beneficiosas porque equilibran la humedad cuando estás cocinando alimentos en la estufa. Ayudan a mantener el sabor y algo de humedad como una tapa completa, pero también permiten que el exceso de humedad se escape – esto dará como resultado un chutney rico y cocido lentamente. Para construir su propio rasgar un cuadrado de su rollo de papel de pergamino (más grande en tamaño que el diámetro de su cacerola). Coloque el papel plano. Doblarlo por la mitad hacia ti. Luego tome el lado izquierdo y doble por la mitad sobre la derecha. Ahora doble las esquinas correctas para encontrarse entre sí. Debería parecer un triángulo (piensa en esto como si estuvieras haciendo un copo de nieve decorativo). Cortar la punta (alrededor de ¼ "lo hará: esto permite la ventilación del vapor en el centro) y mítela en su olla para ver cuánto debe cortarse desde el otro extremo. La tapa debe encajar perfectamente en tu olla para que se sienta encima del chutney.

description: Coconut butter is to coconut oil as butter is to ghee; it’s made from whole coconut flesh, with all the delicious fat and the solids included. The oil and flesh meld together to form a creamy texture that spreads well. I wouldn’t use it for any high heat cooking, though, as the bits of flesh will just burn. Spoonfuls of this stuff are delicious, but addictive. Because the flesh is included, it retains a decent amount of sweetness. A big dollop of coconut butter can really finish off a curry nicely, though. Two tablespoons get you 18 grams fat, 16 saturated. What it is: When coconut oil and coconut meat grind together, they form a peanut butter-like paste called coconut butter (also known as coconut manna). It provides a richer coconut flavor than the oil and texturally feels waxy when cold and creamy when warm. How to store it: Like coconut oil, the butter is solid at room temperature. However, like other nut butters and tahini, the oil and fatty parts may separate. To combine, simply warm the whole jar in a bowl of warm water (or lay it on its side). Then, use a knife or chopstick to stir together. How to use it: Think of coconut butter as a “topper” versus a “cooker.” Spread on crackers or a slice of cake. Stir a little into your coffee as creamer.Let it melt over waffles or make coconut herb butter. A rich and creamy product with a peanut butter-like texture. Unlike coconut oil, the butter actually contains the meat of the coconut so it's more solid and white. It's a common ingredient in the Paleo Diet and Vegan lifestyle and uses for it include replacing other nut butters in baking, spreading on toast, melting and drizzling on desserts, or just eating it straight.

Rainier cherries are a mixed type of cherry derived from crossing Bing and Van sweet cherries. They are very different from common tart cherries both in color and flavor. Whereas tart cherries are bright red, to the point they can be used as food coloring when powdered, organic Rainier cherries are a mix of red and yellow. They are very sweet and “fleshy” when fresh. Sun-dried Rainier cherries have a rich bittersweet, nearly syrupy-sweet flavor. They might remind you of some types of raisins.


Ideas on How to Eat Organic Dried Rainier Cherries

As they are naturally delicious, you can eat sun-dried Rainier cherries right as they are. Keep a pack on hand for when you need a quick energizing snack. But do remind yourself not to overeat this delicious treat.

It’s also a great idea to use dried pitted Rainier cherries when baking. You can add them to cookies, muffins, and fruitcakes. Also, be sure to add some to your homemade granola.

Sprinkle some organic dried Rainier cherries on your cereal in the morning. This will help you if you want to cut down on the sugar as the treat is sweet and will make it easier to cope with unsweetened oatmeal.

Keep your organic Rainier cherries in an airtight container and away from heat. It’s essential to make sure they remain dry. This way, you’ll be able to enjoy them for months.

description:
History of Blueberries Plants

Who doesn’t love blueberries? They are sweet, juicy, and taste incredible in muffins. They are also rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants, which makes these berries one of the delicioust foods you can find.

There are many different types of blueberries plants. They are often called different names and grow all over the world. However, the fruits that are considered ‘blueberries’ in the world of commercial deals, are native to the North America. Here they grow freely and you can still find quite a few bushes producing tasty berries in the wild.

These blueberries have been an exclusively American treasure for a very long time. They only traveled to Europe in the 1930s, but today they are grown in South America, New Zealand, and Australia as well.

The US remains the main producer of blueberries in the world, and Washington is the leader among the states with over 96 million tons of berries produced there every year. Michigan and Georgia are close in their supply rates, but every state grows at least some variety of local blueberries plants, be they cultivated or ‘wild’.

Wild blueberries are smaller, but they are also sold commercially. These berries are harvested from managed, but natural growth areas of the shrubs.

The people of today can thank Frederic Coville and Elizabeth White for the blueberries plants that produce large fruits. In 1910, they started a cultivation program that encouraged everyone to grow their own variety of blueberries, and we get to enjoy its results.

bullet_point: [DELICIOUS SNACK FOR ANY TIME: Eat Organic Dried Rainier Cherries every time you want to enjoy a good and sweet snack., FIBER AND VITAMIN SOURCE: Not only are Organic Rainier Cherries a tasty treat, they are also rich in fiber, as well as iron and vitamin A., NATURALLY SWEET TREAT: Sun-dried Rainier Cherries have a rich bittersweet flavor similar to some raisins., USE IN BAKING: To enjoy the benefits and flavor of Rainier cherries, add them to your muffins and cookies., ADD SWEETNESS TO YOUR OATMEAL: Sprinkle some dried Rainier cherries onto your oatmeal or any other cereal to make it delicious.]
description:
The rich and sweet taste of Organic Dried Rainier Cherries is sure to make you fall in love with this snack. They are not only delicious but also contain a lot of fiber and some vitamin A, iron, and calcium. Organic Rainier Cherries have many culinary uses and you can happily enjoy them every day.

Rainier cherries are a mixed type of cherry derived from crossing Bing and Van sweet cherries. They are very different from common tart cherries both in color and flavor. Whereas tart cherries are bright red, to the point they can be used as food coloring when powdered, organic Rainier cherries are a mix of red and yellow. They are very sweet and “fleshy” when fresh. Sun-dried Rainier cherries have a rich bittersweet, nearly syrupy-sweet flavor. They might remind you of some types of raisins.


Ideas on How to Eat Organic Dried Rainier Cherries

As they are naturally delicious, you can eat sun-dried Rainier cherries right as they are. Keep a pack on hand for when you need a quick energizing snack. But do remind yourself not to overeat this delicious treat.

It’s also a great idea to use dried pitted Rainier cherries when baking. You can add them to cookies, muffins, and fruitcakes. Also, be sure to add some to your homemade granola.

Sprinkle some organic dried Rainier cherries on your cereal in the morning. This will help you if you want to cut down on the sugar as the treat is sweet and will make it easier to cope with unsweetened oatmeal.

Keep your organic Rainier cherries in an airtight container and away from heat. It’s essential to make sure they remain dry. This way, you’ll be able to enjoy them for months.

description:
Pears

There are more than 3,000 varieties grown around the globe, though the best known in the U.S. is the Anjou.

How to ripen

This tree fruit is picked when the fruit is still hard, so it's essential to allow pears to spend a day or two at room temperature in a sealed brown paper bag. Gently press near the stem to test for ripeness. It's ready to eat when the flesh gives a little.

How to store

Place ripe pears in the refrigerator.

How to prep
  • Wash pears in cool, running water
  • Cut the ripe fruit in quarters
  • Run a sharp knife from the stem to the core to remove the seeds
  • Slice or chop, depending on the recipe

Like apples, cut pears darken when exposed to air, so it's important to rub the surface with half a lemon or dunk the fruit briefly in citrus just diluted with a little water.

Chef's tip

Create a memorable flatbread by topping your favorite pizza crust recipe with sliced pears and crumbled blue cheese. Bake in a 400-degree oven for 10-15 minutes and finish with a generous sprinkle of chopped walnuts.

Peras

Hay más de 3.000 variedades cultivadas en todo el mundo, aunque la más conocida en los Estados Unidos es el Anjou.

Cómo madurar

Esta fruta del árbol se recoge cuando la fruta sigue siendo dura, por lo que es esencial permitir que las peras pasen un día o dos a temperatura ambiente en una bolsa de papel marrón sellada. Presione suavemente cerca del tallo para comprobar la madurez. Está listo para comer cuando la carne da un poco.

Cómo almacenar

Coloque las peras maduras en el refrigerador.

Cómo preparar
  • Lavar las peras en agua fría y corriente
  • Cortar la fruta madura en cuartos
  • Ejecutar un cuchillo afilado desde el tallo hasta el núcleo para eliminar las semillas
  • Cortar o picar, dependiendo de la receta

Al igual que las manzanas, las peras cortadas se oscurecen cuando se exponen al aire, por lo que es importante frotar la superficie con medio limón o sumergir la fruta brevemente en cítricos simplemente diluidos con un poco de agua.

Consejo del chef

Crea un pan plano memorable cubriendo tu receta favorita de corteza de pizza con peras en rodajas y queso azul desmenuzado. Hornee en un horno de 400 grados durante 10-15 minutos y termine con un generoso espolvoreo de nueces picadas.

description:
History of Blueberries Plants

Who doesn’t love blueberries? They are sweet, juicy, and taste incredible in muffins. They are also rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants, which makes these berries one of the delicioust foods you can find.

There are many different types of blueberries plants. They are often called different names and grow all over the world. However, the fruits that are considered ‘blueberries’ in the world of commercial deals, are native to the North America. Here they grow freely and you can still find quite a few bushes producing tasty berries in the wild.

These blueberries have been an exclusively American treasure for a very long time. They only traveled to Europe in the 1930s, but today they are grown in South America, New Zealand, and Australia as well.

The US remains the main producer of blueberries in the world, and Washington is the leader among the states with over 96 million tons of berries produced there every year. Michigan and Georgia are close in their supply rates, but every state grows at least some variety of local blueberries plants, be they cultivated or ‘wild’.

Wild blueberries are smaller, but they are also sold commercially. These berries are harvested from managed, but natural growth areas of the shrubs.

The people of today can thank Frederic Coville and Elizabeth White for the blueberries plants that produce large fruits. In 1910, they started a cultivation program that encouraged everyone to grow their own variety of blueberries, and we get to enjoy its results.

description:
Grown and harvested across the Philippines in nutrient-rich sandy soil, our coconuts are carefully selected for their natural flavour and aroma. The tropical climes produce the best harvests with plenty of rain and sun for the coconuts to absorb. The crops are harvested from a tree when it is between 10 and 20 years old.

Our fair trade suppliers are experts in knowing when it is exactly right to harvest the coconuts. When the crop turns from a bright green to a hue of yellow is when they are ready to be harvested. Knowing when to pick the coconut helps to achieve a fruit which is rich in flavour and nutrients.

After the harvest the coconuts are carefully washed, husked and peeled. We are proud to utilise the whole coconut, fibres are saved and passed on to be used in clothing, tableware and other uses, we make sure none of the precious fruit goes to waste.

Each coconut is peeled by hand and halved. The coconut meat is then thoroughly cleaned and grated extra fine. In small batches, the coconut is then gently dried to remove any moisture which stops microbial growth. When the coconut reaches the perfect texture, they are removed from the drier. The coconut is left as unsweetened coconut . Due to our careful selection process and drying, there is no need to sweeten the coconut with added sugars or preservatives, resulting in a healthier product full of nutrients.

Our high quality unsulfered shredded coconut is perfect for use in trail mixes, baked goods and as a garnish.

When it comes to dried mangoes, Cebu City, Philippines comes immediately to mind. The Philippines' wonderful tropical climate is the home of these delectable, addictive food products that are must-haves in every tourists' food souvenir bags to bring home.

For 47-year-old Audrey Regis, she knew she had to set herself apart when she started her own line of delicacies in 2013. As a child, she loved caramel. Chocolate. Caramel. Philippine dried mangoes. It is every sweet tooth's fantasy. As if this was not enough, Audrey's Confectioneries carry four variants: Mango Caramel Classic, Chocolate Mango Caramel, Mango Caramel Cashew, and Mango Caramel Pistachio.

On a diet? Sure, chocolate-covered, mixed-with-caramel mangoes count as FRUIT, so eat as many as you want!

description:
Plantains

Sometimes called “cooking bananas”, this staple of diets in Asia, Africa and Latin America can be prepared and eaten at various stages of ripeness.

How to ripen

It might look like a banana, but plantains are actually a starchy vegetable that's eaten like a potato in many parts of the world. It's picked green and turns a dark brown when it's ripened at room temperature for a day or two, or up to a week.

How to store

Plantains should be stored at room temperature. Once prepped, they should be refrigerated.

How to prep

Plantains peel easily when ripe and must be cooked before eating.

Cut into 2-inch pieces and gently press with the palm of your hand until it forms a flat patty that's fried in olive oil until golden brown.

Chef's tip

Fried plantains are usually paired with succulent roast pork or spicy jerk chicken, but they shine in dessert dishes as well.

Sprinkle slices with a bit of brown sugar and bake at 350 for 10-15 minutes, until soft and golden. Serve with coconut ice cream for a tropical treat.



Plátanos

A veces llamado "cocinar plátanos", este básico de las dietas en Asia, África y América Latina se puede preparar y comer en varias etapas de madurez.

Cómo madurar

Puede parecer un plátano, pero los plátanos son en realidad un vegetal almidonado que se come como una patata en muchas partes del mundo. Se recoge de color verde y se vuelve marrón oscuro cuando está madurado a temperatura ambiente durante un día o dos o hasta una semana.

Cómo almacenar

Los plátanos deben almacenarse a temperatura ambiente. Una vez preparados, deben refrigerarse.

Cómo preparar

Los plátanos se pelan fácilmente cuando están maduros y deben cocinarse antes de comer.

Cortar en trozos de 2.0 in y presionar suavemente con la palma de la mano hasta que forme una empanada plana que se fríe en aceite de oliva hasta que esté dorada.

Consejo del chef

Los plátanos fritos generalmente se emparejan con suculento cerdo asado o pollo picante, pero también brillan en platos de postre.

Espolvoree las rodajas con un poco de azúcar morena y hornee a 350 durante 10-15 minutos, hasta que estén suaves y doradas. Servir con helado de coco para un regalo tropical.

description:
History of Blueberries Plants

Who doesn’t love blueberries? They are sweet, juicy, and taste incredible in muffins. They are also rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants, which makes these berries one of the delicioust foods you can find.

There are many different types of blueberries plants. They are often called different names and grow all over the world. However, the fruits that are considered ‘blueberries’ in the world of commercial deals, are native to the North America. Here they grow freely and you can still find quite a few bushes producing tasty berries in the wild.

These blueberries have been an exclusively American treasure for a very long time. They only traveled to Europe in the 1930s, but today they are grown in South America, New Zealand, and Australia as well.

The US remains the main producer of blueberries in the world, and Washington is the leader among the states with over 96 million tons of berries produced there every year. Michigan and Georgia are close in their supply rates, but every state grows at least some variety of local blueberries plants, be they cultivated or ‘wild’.

Wild blueberries are smaller, but they are also sold commercially. These berries are harvested from managed, but natural growth areas of the shrubs.

The people of today can thank Frederic Coville and Elizabeth White for the blueberries plants that produce large fruits. In 1910, they started a cultivation program that encouraged everyone to grow their own variety of blueberries, and we get to enjoy its results.

At Food To Live, we source our Organic Dried Blueberries from the top-rated farmers and ensure that they are processed with utmost care. Our USDA facility adheres to the high safety standards maintained in the US .

Growing Blueberries at Home

This shrub is so tenacious and adaptable, everyone who has patch of land can grow blueberries plants on their own.

►Cranberries are a member of the heather family and related to blueberries, bilberries, and lingonberries. The most commonly grown species is the North American cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon), but other types are found in nature. ►Fresh cranberries are nearly 90% water, but the rest is mostly carbs and fiber. Cranberries are primarily made up of carbs and fiber. They also boast several vitamins and minerals. Keep in mind that cranberry juice has almost no fiber.

description:
Pears

There are more than 3,000 varieties grown around the globe, though the best known in the U.S. is the Anjou.

How to ripen

This tree fruit is picked when the fruit is still hard, so it's essential to allow pears to spend a day or two at room temperature in a sealed brown paper bag. Gently press near the stem to test for ripeness. It's ready to eat when the flesh gives a little.

How to store

Place ripe pears in the refrigerator.

How to prep
  • Wash pears in cool, running water
  • Cut the ripe fruit in quarters
  • Run a sharp knife from the stem to the core to remove the seeds
  • Slice or chop, depending on the recipe

Like apples, cut pears darken when exposed to air, so it's important to rub the surface with half a lemon or dunk the fruit briefly in citrus just diluted with a little water.

Chef's tip

Create a memorable flatbread by topping your favorite pizza crust recipe with sliced pears and crumbled blue cheese. Bake in a 400-degree oven for 10-15 minutes and finish with a generous sprinkle of chopped walnuts.

Peras

Hay más de 3.000 variedades cultivadas en todo el mundo, aunque la más conocida en los Estados Unidos es el Anjou.

Cómo madurar

Esta fruta del árbol se recoge cuando la fruta sigue siendo dura, por lo que es esencial permitir que las peras pasen un día o dos a temperatura ambiente en una bolsa de papel marrón sellada. Presione suavemente cerca del tallo para comprobar la madurez. Está listo para comer cuando la carne da un poco.

Cómo almacenar

Coloque las peras maduras en el refrigerador.

Cómo preparar
  • Lavar las peras en agua fría y corriente
  • Cortar la fruta madura en cuartos
  • Ejecutar un cuchillo afilado desde el tallo hasta el núcleo para eliminar las semillas
  • Cortar o picar, dependiendo de la receta

Al igual que las manzanas, las peras cortadas se oscurecen cuando se exponen al aire, por lo que es importante frotar la superficie con medio limón o sumergir la fruta brevemente en cítricos simplemente diluidos con un poco de agua.

Consejo del chef

Crea un pan plano memorable cubriendo tu receta favorita de corteza de pizza con peras en rodajas y queso azul desmenuzado. Hornee en un horno de 400 grados durante 10-15 minutos y termine con un generoso espolvoreo de nueces picadas.

This tree fruit is picked when the fruit is still hard, so it's essential to allow pears to spend a day or two at room temperature in a sealed brown paper bag. Gently press near the stem to test for ripeness. It's ready to eat when the flesh gives a little.

How to store

Place ripe pears in the refrigerator.

How to prep
  • Wash pears in cool, running water
  • Cut the ripe fruit in quarters
  • Run a sharp knife from the stem to the core to remove the seeds
  • Slice or chop, depending on the recipe

Like apples, cut pears darken when exposed to air, so it's important to rub the surface with half a lemon or dunk the fruit briefly in citrus just diluted with a little water.

Chef's tip

Create a memorable flatbread by topping your favorite pizza crust recipe with sliced pears and crumbled blue cheese. Bake in a 400-degree oven for 10-15 minutes and finish with a generous sprinkle of chopped walnuts.

description:
A Delicious Selection of Freeze-Dried Fruits.

Why Freeze Dried?
The process of removing the water in fruits using freezing instead of heating is brilliant. Indeed, freeze dried food contains nearly all the nutrients present in the original products as opposed to heat dried products, which are deprived of most of them because of the high temperatures. Freeze drying consists of freezing the fresh produce, then using a vacuum-like process to remove the frozen water in the fruit. That leaves you with delicious fruits full of nutrients that weigh only a very small portion of the original weight and that do not go bad even after many years.

Enjoy a delicious mix of banana, blueberry, cherry, mango, peach, pear, pineapple, raspberry, strawberry, blackberry, fig, apple, lychee, grape and cranberry. Please note that cherries and lychees may contain pits.

title: Green Plantain
bullet_point: [Green plantains should be stored at room temperature until ripe (when they've turned almost completely black), Once ripe, plantains should be store in the refrigerator and used within 1-2 days, Discard peel and be sure to cook before consuming, Plantains can be prepared and served in a variety of delicious dishes, and can be prepared by steaming, frying, or oven-baking]
description:
Plantains

Sometimes called “cooking bananas”, this staple of diets in Asia, Africa and Latin America can be prepared and eaten at various stages of ripeness.

How to ripen

It might look like a banana, but plantains are actually a starchy vegetable that's eaten like a potato in many parts of the world. It's picked green and turns a dark brown when it's ripened at room temperature for a day or two, or up to a week.

How to store

Plantains should be stored at room temperature. Once prepped, they should be refrigerated.

How to prep

Plantains peel easily when ripe and must be cooked before eating.

Cut into 2-inch pieces and gently press with the palm of your hand until it forms a flat patty that's fried in olive oil until golden brown.

Chef's tip

Fried plantains are usually paired with succulent roast pork or spicy jerk chicken, but they shine in dessert dishes as well.

Sprinkle slices with a bit of brown sugar and bake at 350 for 10-15 minutes, until soft and golden. Serve with coconut ice cream for a tropical treat.



Plátanos

A veces llamado "cocinar plátanos", este básico de las dietas en Asia, África y América Latina se puede preparar y comer en varias etapas de madurez.

Cómo madurar

Puede parecer un plátano, pero los plátanos son en realidad un vegetal almidonado que se come como una patata en muchas partes del mundo. Se recoge de color verde y se vuelve marrón oscuro cuando está madurado a temperatura ambiente durante un día o dos o hasta una semana.

Cómo almacenar

Los plátanos deben almacenarse a temperatura ambiente. Una vez preparados, deben refrigerarse.

Cómo preparar

Los plátanos se pelan fácilmente cuando están maduros y deben cocinarse antes de comer.

Cortar en trozos de 2.0 in y presionar suavemente con la palma de la mano hasta que forme una empanada plana que se fríe en aceite de oliva hasta que esté dorada.

Consejo del chef

Los plátanos fritos generalmente se emparejan con suculento cerdo asado o pollo picante, pero también brillan en platos de postre.

Espolvoree las rodajas con un poco de azúcar morena y hornee a 350 durante 10-15 minutos, hasta que estén suaves y doradas. Servir con helado de coco para un regalo tropical.

description:
History of Blueberries Plants

Who doesn’t love blueberries? They are sweet, juicy, and taste incredible in muffins. They are also rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants, which makes these berries one of the delicioust foods you can find.

There are many different types of blueberries plants. They are often called different names and grow all over the world. However, the fruits that are considered ‘blueberries’ in the world of commercial deals, are native to the North America. Here they grow freely and you can still find quite a few bushes producing tasty berries in the wild.

These blueberries have been an exclusively American treasure for a very long time. They only traveled to Europe in the 1930s, but today they are grown in South America, New Zealand, and Australia as well.

The US remains the main producer of blueberries in the world, and Washington is the leader among the states with over 96 million tons of berries produced there every year. Michigan and Georgia are close in their supply rates, but every state grows at least some variety of local blueberries plants, be they cultivated or ‘wild’.

Wild blueberries are smaller, but they are also sold commercially. These berries are harvested from managed, but natural growth areas of the shrubs.

The people of today can thank Frederic Coville and Elizabeth White for the blueberries plants that produce large fruits. In 1910, they started a cultivation program that encouraged everyone to grow their own variety of blueberries, and we get to enjoy its results.

At Food To Live, we source our Organic Dried Blueberries from the top-rated farmers and ensure that they are processed with utmost care. Our USDA facility adheres to the high safety standards maintained in the US .

A Delicious Selection of Freeze-Dried Fruits.

Why Freeze Dried?
The process of removing the water in fruits using freezing instead of heating is brilliant. Indeed, freeze dried food contains nearly all the nutrients present in the original products as opposed to heat dried products, which are deprived of most of them because of the high temperatures. Freeze drying consists of freezing the fresh produce, then using a vacuum-like process to remove the frozen water in the fruit. That leaves you with delicious fruits full of nutrients that weigh only a very small portion of the original weight and that do not go bad even after many years.

bullet_point: [DELICIOUS SNACK FOR ANY TIME: Eat Organic Dried Rainier Cherries every time you want to enjoy a good and sweet snack., FIBER AND VITAMIN SOURCE: Not only are Organic Rainier Cherries a tasty treat, they are also rich in fiber, as well as iron and vitamin A., NATURALLY SWEET TREAT: Sun-dried Rainier Cherries have a rich bittersweet flavor similar to some raisins., USE IN BAKING: To enjoy the benefits and flavor of Rainier cherries, add them to your muffins and cookies., ADD SWEETNESS TO YOUR OATMEAL: Sprinkle some dried Rainier cherries onto your oatmeal or any other cereal to make it delicious.]
description:
The rich and sweet taste of Organic Dried Rainier Cherries is sure to make you fall in love with this snack. They are not only delicious but also contain a lot of fiber and some vitamin A, iron, and calcium. Organic Rainier Cherries have many culinary uses and you can happily enjoy them every day.

Rainier cherries are a mixed type of cherry derived from crossing Bing and Van sweet cherries. They are very different from common tart cherries both in color and flavor. Whereas tart cherries are bright red, to the point they can be used as food coloring when powdered, organic Rainier cherries are a mix of red and yellow. They are very sweet and “fleshy” when fresh. Sun-dried Rainier cherries have a rich bittersweet, nearly syrupy-sweet flavor. They might remind you of some types of raisins.


Ideas on How to Eat Organic Dried Rainier Cherries

As they are naturally delicious, you can eat sun-dried Rainier cherries right as they are. Keep a pack on hand for when you need a quick energizing snack. But do remind yourself not to overeat this delicious treat.

It’s also a great idea to use dried pitted Rainier cherries when baking. You can add them to cookies, muffins, and fruitcakes. Also, be sure to add some to your homemade granola.

Sprinkle some organic dried Rainier cherries on your cereal in the morning. This will help you if you want to cut down on the sugar as the treat is sweet and will make it easier to cope with unsweetened oatmeal.

Keep your organic Rainier cherries in an airtight container and away from heat. It’s essential to make sure they remain dry. This way, you’ll be able to enjoy them for months.

How do Organic Mango Cheeks taste?

Dried mango tastes a bit different from fresh mango, but you can't confuse it with any other fruit; dried variety is much more "concentrated" and much sweeter than mango in season. You can even use these mango cheeks in dishes that you want to sweeten without adding any sweeteners. For example, they will add specks of sweetness to cookies, muffins, and things like oatmeal.


How many calories are in dried mango no sugar added/dried unsweetened mango?

Dried mango cheeks make a great energizing snack or a quick fix to your sugar needs. If you are overseeing your daily calorie intake, you'll need to make sure this kind of sweet supplement fits into your plan. Four organic dried mango slices have around 130 calories. Note that this is the count for unsweetened dried mango. Syrup or honey will add a lot more to that number.


What’s the best way to enjoy organic dried mango slices?

We think the best way to enjoy organic mango cheeks is to eat them as they are, they are delicious and might become your favorite.

description:
Dried Cherries from Food To Live are organic and sourced from the best farmers on the market. We make sure all our suppliers use only the best and safest agricultural practices.


Organic Dried Cherries: Nutrition Data

Cherries are full of valuable nutrients in both raw and dried state. They contain small amounts of almost every essential nutrient.

The elements present in larger amounts include:

● Iron
● Copper
● Manganese
● Potassium
● Vitamin C
● Vitamin A


How to Use

Dried cherries make an extremely versatile cooking ingredient. Unlike many other dried fruits, their tart and rich flavor allows including them in both sweet and savory recipes. You can always enrich the taste of a fresh salad with these tiny fruits.

There is a great number of dried cherries recipes for baked goods that you definitely should try. Dried cherries muffins and cookies taste especially well and make for a great, nutritious snack.

Dried cherries are a fantastic ingredient for granolas and trail mixes.

If you want to make a simple but impressive treat for your family or guests, just coat dried cherries in chocolate.

Storage Guide
Organic Dried Cherries have a very long shelf life by default, and you can increase it greatly. If you want the pack to last as long as possible, you just need to put it in the freezer. Frozen dried fruits won’t spoil for years.
In a sealed package, dried cherries would last for over a year even without the freezer. Although, their shelf life is always extended by the fridge.
Once the package is open, dried cherries should be stored in a cool and dry place, inside an airtight container.

title: Jansal Valley Dried Apple Rings, 4 oz
bullet_point: [Soft and chewy, Deliciously sweet, Add to baked goods or enjoy as a snack, Kosher]
description:
Jansal Valley Dried Apple Rings

Our Jansal Valley Dried Apple Rings begin by using the best fresh fruit handpicked from the world’s finest farms. By using the highest quality ingredients, the fruits natural flavor and sweetness require little else to shine all year round.



Apples a la Mode

This dessert is a take on the classic Apple Pie à la mode. The fresh baked apples give you the creamy texture of apple pie filling and the roasted dried apples crisp up like pie crust. Together, they make a perfect pie substitute with a whole lot less work! This dish is perfect for a last minute dessert or sweet treat! Using raw Turbinado cane sugar gives a subtle molasses flavor and a rustic texture due to its larger crystals.

1 Cup Jansal Valley Dried Apple Rings / roughly chopped

2 Apples (Golden Delicious or Honey Crisp) / roughly chopped / seeds and stem removed

3 T Butter / melted

2 T Raw Turbinado Cane Sugar*

1 t Cinnamon

2 t Lemon Juice / approx. ½ lemon

Parchment Paper*

4 Scoops of Vanilla Ice Cream / Whipped Cream

Optional Topping: Caramel

Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Combine all ingredients into a bowl and toss to coat apples evenly. Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper and arrange the apples in one flat layer. Roast for 12 to 15 minutes or until the fresh apples are tender. Serve the apples in a bowl topped with ice cream and enjoy!

*Tip:

1. Using raw Turbinado cane sugar gives a subtle molasses flavor and a rustic texture due to its larger size crystals.

2. Using Parchment paper preserves your pans and makes clean easy!



Jansal Valley Anillos de manzana seca

Nuestros anillos de manzana seca Jansal Valley comienzan usando la mejor fruta fresca seleccionada a mano de las mejores granjas del mundo. Mediante el uso de ingredientes de la más alta calidad, el sabor natural de las frutas y dulzura requieren poco más para brillar durante todo el año.



Manzanas a la Modo

Este postre es una toma en el clásico Apple Pie à la modo. Las manzanas frescas al horno le dan la textura cremosa del relleno de pastel de manzana y las manzanas secas tostadas crujientes como la corteza de pastel. ¡Juntos, hacen un sustituto perfecto de la tarta con mucho menos trabajo! Este plato es perfecto para un postre de último minuto o un dulce dulce! El uso de azúcar de caña Turbinado crudo da un sutil sabor a melaza y una textura rústica debido a sus cristales más grandes.

1 taza de anillos de manzana seca Jansal Valley.

2 manzanas (Golden Delicious o Miel Crujiente) / ásperamente picadas / semillas y tallos eliminados

3 T Mantequilla / derretida

2 T Azúcar de caña Turbinado Crudo*

1 t Canela

2 t Zumo de Limón / aprox. ½ limón

Papel Pergamino*

4 cucharadas de helado de vainilla/crema batida

Topping opcional: Caramelo

Precaliente el horno a 350 grados F. Combine todos los ingredientes en un recipiente y mezcle para cubrir las manzanas de manera uniforme. Cubra una hoja de galletas con papel de pergamino y coloque las manzanas en una capa plana. Asar durante 12 a 15 minutos o hasta que las manzanas frescas estén tiernas. Sirva las manzanas en un tazón cubierto con helado y disfruta!

*Consejo:

1. El uso de azúcar de caña Turbinado crudo da un sutil sabor a melaza y una textura rústica debido a sus cristales de mayor tamaño.

2. El papel pergamino conserva tus sartenes y facilita la limpieza.

description:
History of Blueberries Plants

Who doesn’t love blueberries? They are sweet, juicy, and taste incredible in muffins. They are also rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants, which makes these berries one of the delicioust foods you can find.

There are many different types of blueberries plants. They are often called different names and grow all over the world. However, the fruits that are considered ‘blueberries’ in the world of commercial deals, are native to the North America. Here they grow freely and you can still find quite a few bushes producing tasty berries in the wild.

These blueberries have been an exclusively American treasure for a very long time. They only traveled to Europe in the 1930s, but today they are grown in South America, New Zealand, and Australia as well.

The US remains the main producer of blueberries in the world, and Washington is the leader among the states with over 96 million tons of berries produced there every year. Michigan and Georgia are close in their supply rates, but every state grows at least some variety of local blueberries plants, be they cultivated or ‘wild’.

Wild blueberries are smaller, but they are also sold commercially. These berries are harvested from managed, but natural growth areas of the shrubs.

The people of today can thank Frederic Coville and Elizabeth White for the blueberries plants that produce large fruits. In 1910, they started a cultivation program that encouraged everyone to grow their own variety of blueberries, and we get to enjoy its results.

At Food To Live, we source our Organic Dried Blueberries from the top-rated farmers and ensure that they are processed with utmost care. Our USDA facility adheres to the high safety standards maintained in the US .

Growing Blueberries at Home

description:
History of Blueberries Plants

Who doesn’t love blueberries? They are sweet, juicy, and taste incredible in muffins. They are also rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants, which makes these berries one of the delicioust foods you can find.

There are many different types of blueberries plants. They are often called different names and grow all over the world. However, the fruits that are considered ‘blueberries’ in the world of commercial deals, are native to the North America. Here they grow freely and you can still find quite a few bushes producing tasty berries in the wild.

These blueberries have been an exclusively American treasure for a very long time. They only traveled to Europe in the 1930s, but today they are grown in South America, New Zealand, and Australia as well.

The US remains the main producer of blueberries in the world, and Washington is the leader among the states with over 96 million tons of berries produced there every year. Michigan and Georgia are close in their supply rates, but every state grows at least some variety of local blueberries plants, be they cultivated or ‘wild’.

Wild blueberries are smaller, but they are also sold commercially. These berries are harvested from managed, but natural growth areas of the shrubs.

The people of today can thank Frederic Coville and Elizabeth White for the blueberries plants that produce large fruits. In 1910, they started a cultivation program that encouraged everyone to grow their own variety of blueberries, and we get to enjoy its results.

At Food To Live, we source our Organic Dried Blueberries from the top-rated farmers and ensure that they are processed with utmost care. Our USDA facility adheres to the high safety standards maintained in the US .

Growing Blueberries at Home

This shrub is so tenacious and adaptable, everyone who has patch of land can grow blueberries plants on their own.

description: Where Do Plums Come From? The plum tree, which bears plum fruits, has been one of the first plants domesticated by our ancestors. People have been growing various varieties of plums all over the world for millennia and archeologists have found the pits that data back as far as 6000 years. Organic Dried Plums from Food To Live allow you to partake in the time-honored tradition of enjoying this incredible fruit in various sweet and savory dishes. Over 40% of the dried plums available on the world market today come from California, where the climate is perfect for cultivating amazingly delicious plum species. Food To Live Dried Plum: Benefit of Organic Product Organic Dried Plums from Food To Live are a safe top-quality product free of any harmful contaminants. They are grown without the use of pesticides, insecticides, and synthetic fertilizers that poison the soil. We make sure that our dried plums are nutritious and safe. This fruit poses a minimal risk of allergy, which means that even babies can enjoy it. Are Dried Plums Prunes? Don’t get confused when you see terms ‘dried plums’ and ‘prunes’. Those products are basically the same thing, so the terms are often used interchangeably. The trick here is that all types of dried plums used to be called prunes, and this name is still the most popular option in Europe and Asia. However, it has fallen out of favor in the US, because marketing studies showed that a major group of consumers (women, age 25-54) has a subconscious negative reaction to the word. Therefore, the term ‘dried plum’ is the more common in America and it’s gradually winning the leading position in the world. There is also a consideration of the plum species. There is a type of prune plum, which should reasonably be called a prune in either fresh or dried state. However, this distinction is mostly overlooked. Oranges

The world's most popular citrus fruit is widely grown in Florida, Texas, and California.

How to ripen

This citrus fruit that's a Vitamin C superstar is harvested when it's ripe, so it's ready to eat when you get it.

How to store

Place this colorful fruit in the refrigerator to extend its life.

How to prep

Wash oranges under cool, running water. This highly portable snack can be easily be peeled and eaten on the go, but to give an orange the supreme treatment slice the top and the bottom of the orange and removing the peel by slicing carefully between the juicy flesh and the white pith. After that's removed, use a small paring knife to cut between the fruit and the membrane. A slice should pop right out, so do this prepping project over a bowl.

Chef's tip

description:
The rich and sweet taste of Organic Dried Rainier Cherries is sure to make you fall in love with this snack. They are not only delicious but also contain a lot of fiber and some vitamin A, iron, and calcium. Organic Rainier Cherries have many culinary uses and you can happily enjoy them every day.

Rainier cherries are a mixed type of cherry derived from crossing Bing and Van sweet cherries. They are very different from common tart cherries both in color and flavor. Whereas tart cherries are bright red, to the point they can be used as food coloring when powdered, organic Rainier cherries are a mix of red and yellow. They are very sweet and “fleshy” when fresh. Sun-dried Rainier cherries have a rich bittersweet, nearly syrupy-sweet flavor. They might remind you of some types of raisins.


Ideas on How to Eat Organic Dried Rainier Cherries

As they are naturally delicious, you can eat sun-dried Rainier cherries right as they are. Keep a pack on hand for when you need a quick energizing snack. But do remind yourself not to overeat this delicious treat.

It’s also a great idea to use dried pitted Rainier cherries when baking. You can add them to cookies, muffins, and fruitcakes. Also, be sure to add some to your homemade granola.

Sprinkle some organic dried Rainier cherries on your cereal in the morning. This will help you if you want to cut down on the sugar as the treat is sweet and will make it easier to cope with unsweetened oatmeal.

Keep your organic Rainier cherries in an airtight container and away from heat. It’s essential to make sure they remain dry. This way, you’ll be able to enjoy them for months.

Place this colorful fruit in the refrigerator to extend its life.

Wash oranges under cool, running water. Sultanas are the original Turkish dried white grape – specifically the dried Thompson Seedless grape, which originated in the part of Turkey that lies on the Asian continent.

In the US, they are often not differentiated from raisins (and are even named as such), despite the fact that they are a different variety of grape which, in its dried form, is plumper, sweeter and juicier than a raisin.

description:
History of Blueberries Plants

Who doesn’t love blueberries? They are sweet, juicy, and taste incredible in muffins. They are also rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants, which makes these berries one of the delicioust foods you can find.

There are many different types of blueberries plants. They are often called different names and grow all over the world. However, the fruits that are considered ‘blueberries’ in the world of commercial deals, are native to the North America. Here they grow freely and you can still find quite a few bushes producing tasty berries in the wild.

These blueberries have been an exclusively American treasure for a very long time. They only traveled to Europe in the 1930s, but today they are grown in South America, New Zealand, and Australia as well.

The US remains the main producer of blueberries in the world, and Washington is the leader among the states with over 96 million tons of berries produced there every year. Michigan and Georgia are close in their supply rates, but every state grows at least some variety of local blueberries plants, be they cultivated or ‘wild’.

Wild blueberries are smaller, but they are also sold commercially. These berries are harvested from managed, but natural growth areas of the shrubs.

The people of today can thank Frederic Coville and Elizabeth White for the blueberries plants that produce large fruits. In 1910, they started a cultivation program that encouraged everyone to grow their own variety of blueberries, and we get to enjoy its results.

At Food To Live, we source our Organic Dried Blueberries from the top-rated farmers and ensure that they are processed with utmost care. Our USDA facility adheres to the high safety standards maintained in the US .

Growing Blueberries at Home

This shrub is so tenacious and adaptable, everyone who has patch of land can grow blueberries plants on their own.

About Our Premium Golden Raisins

Raisins are made by dehydrating green grapes. In most raisins, the drying process oxidizes the grapes and the raisins end up a dark brown/purple/black color. They are left with a warm, malted, honey taste. However, a few varieties like Muscata, Black Monukka, or Sultana keep their light tan color. They have slightly brighter, fruity sweetness to them. The raisins have been dried to the point that they have less than 19% moisture by weight. They have a light golden color, sweet caramel-like flavor, and soft chewy texture. All-natural with no sugar added, a delicious and healthy snack.

Benefits of Raisins

Raisins contain four times the fiber, minerals, and vitamins of fresh grapes. Packed with fiber and potassium as well as powerful antioxidants. Raisins may improve your digestive health and blood sugar levels, decrease inflammation, and lower your blood pressure; however, they should be eaten in moderation because they are high in sugar and calories. Raisins are a useful addition to savory dishes that would benefit from one sweet flavor note. Brussels sprouts, sautéed spinach, and roasted cauliflower are all vegetables that are complimented by raisins.

Storing Raisins

Golden raisins have a very long and stable shelf life if stored in a cool, dry place.

Crystalized Dried Ginger

Crystallized Ginger (also called by some Candied Ginger or Glace Ginger) is pungent with a spicy sweet flavor. Identifiable by its yellowish color, it is often added to baked goods or meals but can also be enjoyed alone. Crystallized ginger tastes both spicy and sweet at the same time. First there is a familiar sweetness on your taste buds and then the heat takes over, but it is not an overwhelming heat. It is pungent and penetrating.

Dried Ginger Benefits

Candied ginger has been used for many years as a natural medicine ingredient. It is most well-known for the calming effects it has on nausea and upset stomachs and is the key ingredient for the popular drink, ginger ale. Ginger is made up of 1% to 4% of essential oil, but that amount depends on the variety. Giving ginger its scent is the sesquiterpenes, which makes up most of the essential oil.

bullet_point: [Can be eaten by itself or used in desserts, salads, snacks and soups, Can be stored at room temperature when whole, once sliced be sure to wrap and store in the refrigerator, Grown in United States or Mexico]
description:
Honeydew Melon

Originally from France, its sweet-sounding moniker is actually a nickname. It was originally known as a White Antibes melon.

How to ripen

This pale green gem gets a little sweeter if left at room temperature for a day or two.

To speed up the process, wrap the honeydew in newspaper.

How to store

Once ripe, honeydew should be stored in the refrigerator.

How to prep
  • Wash melon under cool, running water and pat dry
  • Cut in half, lengthwise
  • Remove the seeds with a spoon

The honeydew is ready to eat, or it can be stored in a sealed container in the refrigerator.

Chef's tip

Add coconut milk and lime zest to a chopped honeydew for a refreshing fruit salad that might be mistaken for dessert.



Melón de Honeydew

Originario de Francia, su apodo de sonido dulce es en realidad un apodo. Originalmente era conocido como melón blanco Antibes.

Cómo madurar

Esta gema verde pálido se vuelve un poco más dulce si se deja a temperatura ambiente durante un día o dos.

Para acelerar el proceso, envuelva el rocío de miel en el periódico.

Cómo almacenar

Una vez maduro, la miel debe almacenarse en el refrigerador.

Cómo preparar
  • Lavar el melón con agua fresca y seca con palmaditas
  • Corte por la mitad, longitudinalmente
  • Retire las semillas con una cuchara

La miel está lista para comer, o puede almacenarse en un recipiente sellado en el refrigerador.

Consejo del chef

Agregue la leche de coco y la ralladura de lima a una miel picada para una ensalada de frutas refrescante que podría confundirse con el postre.

description: Persea Americana, or the Avocado, likely originated in the Tehuacan Valley in the state of Puebla, Mexico. The oldest discovery of an avocado pit comes from Coxcatlan Cave, dating from around 9,000 to 10,000 years ago, although fossil evidence suggests similar species were widespread millions of years ago. The fruit of the plant, also called an avocado (or avocado pear or alligator pear), is botanically a large berry containing a single large seed. The Hass Avocado is currently the most common cultivar of avocado. It produces fruit year-round and accounts for 80% of cultivated avocados in the world. All 'Hass' trees are descended from a single Mother Tree raised by a mail carrier named Rudolph Hass, of La Habra Heights, California. Hass patented the productive tree in 1935. The mother tree unfortunately died and was cut down in September 2002. Hass Avocados have medium-sized oval fruit with a black, pebbled skin. The flesh has a nutty, rich flavor with 19% oil. The fruit of the Hass Avocado has a markedly higher fat content than most other fruit, mostly healthy monounsaturated fat, and as such serves as an important staple in the diet of consumers who have limited access to other foods. Oranges

The world's most popular citrus fruit is widely grown in Florida, Texas, and California.

How to ripen

This citrus fruit that's a Vitamin C superstar is harvested when it's ripe, so it's ready to eat when you get it.

How to store

Place this colorful fruit in the refrigerator to extend its life.

How to prep

Wash oranges under cool, running water. This highly portable snack can be easily be peeled and eaten on the go, but to give an orange the supreme treatment slice the top and the bottom of the orange and removing the peel by slicing carefully between the juicy flesh and the white pith. After that's removed, use a small paring knife to cut between the fruit and the membrane. A slice should pop right out, so do this prepping project over a bowl.

Description/Taste The Fuerte avocado is often recognized as the archetypal avocado, green in color, pear-like in shape, and ranging from six to twelve ounces in size. It has smooth, medium-thin skin that peels easily, with dense, pale green flesh. It is marginally oily with a rich, creamy flavor and notes of hazelnut, and it is still considered by many to be the best tasting avocado. The Fuerte avocado tree is large and spreading, one of the more cold-hardy varieties, and the leaves have a strong anise smell when crushed. The fruit set of the tree is irregular, as some trees never seem to have much fruit while others are productive, and it has a tendency to alternate in bearing, producing an adequate crop every other year, depending on weather at setting time, along with other factors. Avocado trees differ in the types of flowers that they have. Type A have female flowers in the morning and male pollen-producing flowers in the afternoon, and Type B, like the Fuerte avocado, are the opposite. Fruit set in Fuerte avocado trees often improves dramatically when the trees are inter-planted with varieties that have Type A flowers because more pollen is available. When temperatures are less than ideal for fruit set, Fuerte avocado trees may form fruits that are stimulated to grow by the pollen tube but never undergo fertilization, resulting in small, narrow seedless fruit called “cukes”, which may be harvested and sold as cocktail avocados. Unlike most fruits, the avocado does not ripen on the tree and instead begins to ripen once harvested, and their sugar level actually decreases as they mature. Their skin remains green, and the fruit will yield to gentle pressure when ripe.

This bright yellow citrus fruit is harvested when ripe, so it is ready to use immediately.

Lemons can be stored in the refrigerator, uncovered.

How to prep

Wash lemons under cool, running water before slicing, juicing, or grating zest.

When juicing, bring the lemon to room temperature and roll it on the counter to extract more juice.

When slicing into wedges, be sure and remove the seeds.

Chef's tip

description:
History of Blueberries Plants

Who doesn’t love blueberries? They are sweet, juicy, and taste incredible in muffins. They are also rich in essential nutrients and antioxidants, which makes these berries one of the delicioust foods you can find.

There are many different types of blueberries plants. They are often called different names and grow all over the world. However, the fruits that are considered ‘blueberries’ in the world of commercial deals, are native to the North America. Here they grow freely and you can still find quite a few bushes producing tasty berries in the wild.

These blueberries have been an exclusively American treasure for a very long time. They only traveled to Europe in the 1930s, but today they are grown in South America, New Zealand, and Australia as well.

The US remains the main producer of blueberries in the world, and Washington is the leader among the states with over 96 million tons of berries produced there every year. Michigan and Georgia are close in their supply rates, but every state grows at least some variety of local blueberries plants, be they cultivated or ‘wild’.

Wild blueberries are smaller, but they are also sold commercially. These berries are harvested from managed, but natural growth areas of the shrubs.

The people of today can thank Frederic Coville and Elizabeth White for the blueberries plants that produce large fruits. In 1910, they started a cultivation program that encouraged everyone to grow their own variety of blueberries, and we get to enjoy its results.

At Food To Live, we source our Organic Dried Blueberries from the top-rated farmers and ensure that they are processed with utmost care. Our USDA facility adheres to the high safety standards maintained in the US .

Growing Blueberries at Home

This shrub is so tenacious and adaptable, everyone who has patch of land can grow blueberries plants on their own.

Food to Live California Organic Raisins have a long shelf life, so buying in bulk is wise. You can eat them as a snack or use the sultana for cooking. Try this great recipe of raisins muffins:

- 3 tsp baking powder
- 1 ¾ cup all-purpose flour
- ¾ tsp salt
- 1 egg
- ¼ sugar
- 1 zested orange
- 1/3 cup vegetable oil
- ¼ cup orange juice
- ½ cup milk
- ¾ cup raisins

5. Add the raisins and mix.

Did you know that there is a large triangular valley in central Asia that is considered one of the most fertile places in the world? It is a wonder of geography because it is located in a region that is otherwise very dry. There are two things that make the Ferghana valley so fertile.
First is the location between two mountain ranges, the Tien-Shan in the north and the Gissar-Alai in the south, which provide run-off water into the valley from rain and snow. Second are the two rivers running through it, the Naryn and the Kara Darya, which run from east to west.

Hass avocados are the most popular variety in the US. This avocado’s flesh is a yellow-green color and has a luscious, buttery consistency and a subtle nutty flavor.

bullet_point: [Zibibbo raisins with all the nuance of a great glass of wine, Great paired with nuts as an energetic treat or a a sweet elegant accompaniment for your next cheese board, Naturally dried in the powerful Sicilian sun, Zibibbo grape is used to make the famous sweet dessert wine Passito di Pantelleria, In a glass jar of 200 g - 7 oz]
description: Deliciously sweet and tangy, Zibibbo raisins have a soft, meaty texture with tiny seeds that give them a slight crunch. We’re sure they have the most complex flavors of any raisin you’ve ever tried, with all the nuance of a great glass of wine. These raisins are so unique you’ll love snacking on them right out of the bag, but they’re also great paired with nuts as an energetic treat, or as a sweet elegant accompaniment for your next cheese board. Have a deeply complex flavor, that recalls the complexity of wine flavors. Zibibbo - also known as Muscat of Alexandria - is a large grape indigenous to north Africa and Pantelleria, a tiny island in the Mediterranean between Sicilia and Tunisia. Cultivation of Zibibbo grapes dates back to the time of the Phoenicians, but on Pantelleria, the intense heat and volcanic soil create the perfect sweet and tangy fruit. These La Nicchia Uva Passa Zibibbo are naturally dried in the powerful Sicilian sun, just as the people of Pantelleria have been doing for generations. And we’re not the only ones who believe these raisins are epically special. Zibibbo farming in Pantelleria, passed down through generations of vine growers, is the first agricultural activity to ever be included in the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list. In Pantelleria, the Zibibbo grape is used to make the famous sweet dessert wine Passito di Pantelleria, dried to make Zibibbo raisins, and reduced to make Zibibbo Elixir. However you enjoy them, you’ll be tasting a tradition hundreds of years in the making.La Nicchia was founded in 1949 when Antonio Bonomo and Girolamo Giglio began producing capers on Pantelleria. Their children are committed to carrying on their work, and have entrusted the production to Gabriele Lasagni, whose passion for the study of Pantelleria’s raw materials echoes the founders’ devotion to the island and its natural resources.

We’re dedicated to supplying you with extraordinary wholesale nuts and dried fruit at the lowest prices possible.

About Our Premium Golden Raisins

Raisins are made by dehydrating green grapes. In most raisins, the drying process oxidizes the grapes and the raisins end up a dark brown/purple/black color. They are left with a warm, malted, honey taste. However, a few varieties like Muscata, Black Monukka, or Sultana keep their light tan color. They have slightly brighter, fruity sweetness to them. The raisins have been dried to the point that they have less than 19% moisture by weight. They have a light golden color, sweet caramel-like flavor, and soft chewy texture. All-natural with no sugar added, a delicious and healthy snack.

Benefits of Raisins

Raisins contain four times the fiber, minerals, and vitamins of fresh grapes. Packed with fiber and potassium as well as powerful antioxidants. Raisins may improve your digestive health and blood sugar levels, decrease inflammation, and lower your blood pressure; however, they should be eaten in moderation because they are high in sugar and calories. Raisins are a useful addition to savory dishes that would benefit from one sweet flavor note. Brussels sprouts, sautéed spinach, and roasted cauliflower are all vegetables that are complimented by raisins.

Storing Raisins

Golden raisins have a very long and stable shelf life if stored in a cool, dry place.

description:
Plums

The trees that bear this delicious fruit first appeared in California in the late 1800s, transplants from Asia. Plums are believed to be one of the first foods cultivated, though the tree's origin remains a mystery.

How to ripen

This tree fruit is an ideal candidate for spending some time in a sealed brown paper bag, where it will sweeten and soften in a day or two.

How to store

Place ripe fruit in a plastic bag in the refrigerator.

How to prep

Most often eaten in a series of dripping-down-your-chin juicy bites, plums are also a snap to make recipe ready.

  • Wash under cool, running water
  • Cut in half length-wise and gently twist to separate
  • Remove pit and then chop or slice to serve in salads or yogurt
Chef's tip

A plum's natural beauty makes it a prime candidate for showing off in a rustic, open-faced tart. Take a shortcut by using slightly thawed puff pastry dough.

  • Roll the piece of pastry dough out until it has expanded about 2-inches
  • Transfer to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper
  • Brush the dough with your favorite jam
  • Arrange sliced plums on top, leaving a 2-inch perimeter
  • Gently fold the edges of the dough over part of the fruit
  • Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon of sugar and bake in a pre-heated 400 degree oven for 25-30 minutes
  • Cool slightly before cutting to serve


Ciruelas

Los árboles que llevan esta deliciosa fruta aparecieron por primera vez en California a finales de 1800, trasplantes de Asia. Se cree que las ciruelas son uno de los primeros alimentos cultivados, aunque el origen del árbol sigue siendo un misterio.

Cómo madurar

Esta fruta de árbol es un candidato ideal para pasar algún tiempo en una bolsa de papel marrón sellada, donde endulzará y suavizará en un día o dos.

Cómo almacenar

Coloque la fruta madura en una bolsa de plástico en el refrigerador.

Cómo preparar

La mayoría de las veces se come en una serie de bocados jugosos que gotean hacia abajo de la barbilla, las ciruelas también son un complemento para preparar la receta.

  • Lavar con agua fría y corriente.
  • Corte a la mitad de la longitud y gire suavemente para separarlo.
  • Retire el pozo y luego picar o rebanar para servir en ensaladas o yogur
Consejo del chef

La belleza natural de una ciruela lo convierte en un candidato privilegiado para presumir en una tarta rústica de cara abierta. Tome un atajo usando masa de hojaldre ligeramente descongelada.

  • Enrolla el trozo de masa de masa hasta que se haya expandido alrededor de 2 pulgadas
  • Transfiera a una bandeja para hornear forrada con papel pergamino
  • Cepille la masa con su mermelada favorita
  • Organizar ciruelas en rodajas en la parte superior, dejando un perímetro de 2 pulgadas
  • Dobla suavemente los bordes de la masa sobre parte de la fruta
  • Espolvorear con 1 cucharada de azúcar y hornear en un horno precalentado a 400 grados durante 25-30 minutos
  • Enfriar ligeramente antes de cortar para servir.

description:
Sweet and slightly tangy, SHILOH FARMS Turkish Apricots are great, chewy treat to be enjoyed right out of the bag! Their rich, apricot flavor will also make them a favorite for baking and cooking purposes. Unsulphered, unsweetened, and pitted*, these apricots are an excellent source of vital nutrients, including iron and Vitamin A.

More commonly found than California Apricots, Turkish varieties have a subtler flavor and less natural acidity. This makes them well-suited for baking and use in dishes where you want other flavors to have a starring role.

To Rehydrate: Simmer fruit in small amount of water or fruit juice approximately 15 minutes, or until tender. Alternately, soak in water or fruit juice in refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight.

Suggestions:
1. Dried apricots are often stewed alone or with other dried fruits and served for breakfast.
2. Finely dice Turkish Apricots and add to cereals (hot or cold) or yogurt.
3. They make a great side dish when cooked along with roasted chicken or lamb.
4. Chop and mix with rice or bread stuffing for poultry.
5. Add to rice, bulgur pilaf, or couscous.
6. Reconstituted apricots can be pureed and spooned over cake or frozen yogurt.
7. Consider dicing and adding them to winter fruit salads, trail mixes, cereals, and baked goods.

How do Organic Mango Cheeks taste?

Dried mango tastes a bit different from fresh mango, but you can't confuse it with any other fruit; dried variety is much more "concentrated" and much sweeter than mango in season. You can even use these mango cheeks in dishes that you want to sweeten without adding any sweeteners. For example, they will add specks of sweetness to cookies, muffins, and things like oatmeal.


How many calories are in dried mango no sugar added/dried unsweetened mango?

Dried mango cheeks make a great energizing snack or a quick fix to your sugar needs. If you are overseeing your daily calorie intake, you'll need to make sure this kind of sweet supplement fits into your plan. Four organic dried mango slices have around 130 calories. Note that this is the count for unsweetened dried mango. Syrup or honey will add a lot more to that number.


What’s the best way to enjoy organic dried mango slices?

We think the best way to enjoy organic mango cheeks is to eat them as they are, they are delicious and might become your favorite.

Using them in baked goods is also a great idea; they will add not only sweetness but also mango flavor to anything. Add some to homemade sweets and granola or experiment with packets of dried cereal and trail mixes when going on the road trip or hiking.

Energy balls with mango pieces mixed with dates and nuts are another tasty idea with a lot of room to create.

description:
Apples

One of the most popular, and diverse, fruits in America is known for being crisp, juicy and full of healthy benefits.

How to store

The tree fruit that's as American as, well... apple pie is harvested in the fall, when various varieties grown in the U.S. are at the peak of freshness.

To ensure this nutritional powerhouse maintains its crispness and juicy, sweet quality, it's essential to store apples in a cool, dark place. The produce drawer in your refrigerator is the perfect place for storing apples you plan to eat within a couple of weeks.

Wrap each piece of fruit in parchment or waxed paper to preserve them even longer.

How to prep

Apples should be washed just prior to eating. To wash, rub apple under running water or scrub with a clean vegetable brush. Pat dry with a clean towel.

The snowy white flesh of an apple turns brown quickly once it's sliced, so toss in a little lemon juice before using in sweet or savory recipes.

No matter how you enjoy them, be sure and rinse apples under a stream of cool water before eating.

Chef's tip

Prized for being amazingly versatile in the kitchen, apples play a starring role in down-home pies and elegant tarts, but they also make a fine addition to salads. Try adding a sliced apple to greens with pecans, blue cheese, and your favorite vinaigrette.

description:
Kiwifruit

This golf ball-size fruit was rebranded with its current name when it first hit U.S. markets in the 1960s. A vitamin powerhouse, it has more than 200 percent of the daily requirement of Vitamin C.

How to ripen

This fuzzy fruit sweetens after a day or two at room temperature.

How to store

Kiwi lasts up to two months when kept in a sealed plastic bag in the refrigerator.

How to prep

Wash the fruit under cool, running water and then it's as simple as slicing:

  • Slice the kiwi in half
  • Run a knife under the skin to release the fruit

The skin of the kiwi is edible, though some recipes call for it to be removed.

Chef's tip

Mash a few slices of peeled kiwi into vinaigrette to add a note of sweetness and an interesting texture to tossed salads.



Kiwi

Cómo madurar

Esta fruta difusa endulza después de un día o dos a temperatura ambiente.

Cómo almacenar

Kiwi dura hasta dos meses cuando se guarda en una bolsa de plástico sellada en el refrigerador.

These moist, sweet treats are great for cooking or snacking straight out of the bag. What is Dried Fruit? Dried fruit is fresh fruit that has been dried naturally in the sun or in dehydration machines. Moisture is removed from the fresh fruit, which makes it more portable and convenient than fresh fruit. However, it does not remove the natural vitamins and antioxidants, making dried fruit as healthy and good for you as fresh fruit! What is the proper way to store my dried fruit? Mariani product should be resealed when not being used, and ideally stored at room temperature. Mariani products can also be refrigerated, but it’s not necessary to do so. The beauty of dried fruit is that it can withstand varying degrees of temperature and still taste great. Keep a bag in your car, backpack, locker or anywhere you need to grab a quick snack. Are your products available in other countries? Yes. The Mariani brand can be found in the UK, Taiwan, Japan, Mexico, Canada, Australia, Italy, Norway, Sweden, Hong Kong and Thailand. Additionally, our products are used as ingredients in the most popular brands of cereals and baked goods throughout the world. How do I know when my dried fruit is too old to eat? All Mariani products have a BEST BEFORE date located on the back of the packages. The month and year lists the ideal shelf life of the fruit. Are your products Kosher approved? Most of our products are kosher certified by the Orthodox Union. Just look for the circle U symbol next to the product name on the front of our products.
